recipes.name: Broken Spaghetti Risotto
ingredients_raw: 8 ounces uncooked spaghetti, broken into 1 inch pieces
0.5 teaspoon red pepper flakes, or to taste
2 tablespoons freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, or to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add spaghetti and toast, stirring constantly, until golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes.
Stir garlic into spaghetti pieces and cook for 30 seconds.

Pour in 1/2 cup broth and increase heat to medium-high. Stir spaghetti and broth until all the liquid is absorbed, 2 to 3 minutes. Repeat this process until all of the stock is absorbed and noodles are desired tenderness, about 10 minutes.
Reduce heat to low. Season spaghetti with red pepper flakes and salt to taste. Remove from heat.
Stir Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese and parsley into spaghetti and serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Broken Spaghetti Risotto
raw_recipe.description: This unique noodle risotto dish is made in the risotto style: toasting the pasta to a delicious nut-brown and adding flavorful broth in increments.

review.reviewBody: OK, I could've totally ate this entire thing, lol...YES, IT'S THAT GOOD! Just be prepared...this took more time (and broth) than called for, which was no problem for me b/c I had the extra time, and this is soooo worth it, just wanting to let others know! Great flavor and method...I used 'Barilla Cut Spaghetti', instead of breaking my own, just b/c I had it. I will be making this over and over~YUM! Thanks for sharing. :)

I have prepared this a couple of times, first following the directions and then “free styling it” a bit. The first time tasted very nice. I used angel hair pasta, as that was all I had.
Then, the second time I added some of the Ladolemono to the pan while browning the broken pasta. Even better.
Then, I cooked a thinly sliced onion in a separate pan until soft, added some shrimp while browning the pasta, adding in chopped sweet peppers in the final moments. I also used the Ladolemono into the vegetables and shrimp. Combined the finished pasta to the shrimp mixture and MDH and I dove in. 
I know, making revisions and then rating is not looked upon with favor, but let me say my rating on this recipe is for the recipe as written. It is a 4 star. It is one of those recipes that makes a cook wonder, ”If I add ??, how will that taste? The additions of Ladolemono, onions peppers and shrimp made a lovely, lemony dish. 
Oh, someone made the suggestion to break the pasta inside a zip bag. Brilliant, as MDH was getting very exasperated with broken bits of pasta flying around the kitchen during my earlier cooking efforts. A muttering husband in the background while cooking is not conducive to cooking genius.
So, original recipe is a 4 star. My free styling recipe is up to you how you rate it. But, please enjoy and thanks for sharing all the recipes.

We tweaked ours a bit by adding 1 cup of chopped baby Bella mushrooms during the initial broth addition, and 1/2 cup of extra broth. We also finished it off with some toasted almond slivers, turned out wonderfully!

This was very easy and quick. I made this just as written but adjusted for 3 people. I found cut fideo in my local market so I used that instead of breaking spaghetti. I needed about 3 1/2 cups of broth to get the pasta al dente for 3 servings. Once it was done I tasted it and it was good as is but it tasted flat. I used homemade chicken broth so the dish needed more salt - about 1 tsp. It still tasted too lean for a main dish so I stirred in 2 tablespoons of butter. With the addition of more parm at serving it was very tasty. Next time I think I will add the salt with the broth so the pasta absorbs the salt for more flavor throughout. Will definitely make again with my changes.

This dish is amazing as is. But, I prefer to make a few changes and turn it into a lovely entree. I chop about half of a medium onion, slice some mushrooms, an additional clove or two of garlic and slice a chicken breast into cubes. Cook the onion in two tablespoons of olive oil until it starts to soften. Add some of the garlic and let cook for a minute or so, then add the chicken. When the chicken is about halfway cooked, add the mushrooms and a sprinkle of red pepper flakes. Let this all cook together, stirring occasionally until the chicken is cooked through. Remove this mixture from the pan and set aside. I then prepare the pasta exactly as described in this recipe. When the pasta is almost done, add the chicken mixture back to the pan. Throw in a handful of pine nuts and cook until the noodles are at your desired texture. Remove from heat, sprinkle with parsley and cheese and serve. I have served this to many guests and received rave reviews. Another awesome Chef John recipe!

I am giving this a 5 for such great flavor. Not sure where I went wrong but the spaghetti just did not want to become tender. I used thin so not sure. I ended up using a lot more broth and covering for a few minutes and it finally cooperated. I stirred in roasted zucchini and mushrooms at the end. and more cheese then suggested. The possibilities are endless. Delicious

Wonderful simple recipe! Be careful with those red pepper flakes though y’all! I added too much and tasted too spicy. To balance it out I added a teaspoon of white sugar and a table spoon of butter and a tablespoon of heavy cream. The flavor evened out with those added. I also added diced tomatoes, about a quarter cup. It turned out great, I love the nutty taste of the toasted spaghetti noddles! 5 stars, will make it again.

In a word, AWESOME. I made this for dinner last evening as a side dish with some greek baked chicken breasts and a green salad for some colour. This is very easy and I normally would make a recipe without changes first time around but, as I always read reviews first, another reviewer said they added mushrooms and onions. I added some sliced fresh mushrooms because they needed to be used and a sliced onion. I sauteed them first and set them aside while I followed the recipe then put them back in at the end to reheat. As other reviewers have said, it does take a little longer to cook than the stated time, maybe 10 minutes. This is a very delicious dish and I will make it again with or without the additions. I love it when I am a hero in the kitchen!

Simple and delicious! I ended up squeezing some lemon slices (about 3-4) for this dish, which added a very lemony fragrance and taste—it was wonderful! Also added some shrimp (and a total of five garlic) into the recipe. In the chicken broth, I used regular stock with added onions. I don't know how the original tastes, but I like my tweaked version. Would definitely make it again! ;}

Good basic recipe but not much in it. The nutty flavor of the pasta was excellent, though. I added some grape tomatoes cut in half, chopped asparagus, some diced bell pepper and shrimp. Knocked it outta the park!

I really liked this as a side dish but did find it needed a little punch of something at the end. Be prepared to just add chicken broth as needed (I used way more than 1.5 cups). Probably depends on the thickness of your broken spaghetti. I loved the nutty/buttery flavor of browning the pasta, but wanted a little more interest. This is a great base for putting just about anything. I added some pine nuts and chopped green onions and it was definitely a keeper.
Its really good

To the lady who wondered why her spaghetti did not get done. Thin spaghetti won't work. The recipe was for cut spaghetti, also called fideo, which is vermicelli. The recipe said you could just break your own spaghetti without telling you what size. I would actually use angel hair, just to make extra sure it gets as done as I want it because I don't like al dente.
So easy, fast and DELISH! Definately a keeper. I didn't have parsley so subbed it with fresh basil. So so good 👍
the kids Loved it! I might have OD'd on the cheese a little, but I put it next to some breaded baked chicken tenders and the kids were in dinner heaven.

I wasted spaghetti, chicken broth and garlic to name a few…and most of all my time. It was bland and boring even though I added red pepper flakes and parmigiana-reggiano cheese. Again, it was a waste of my precious time. “Quote the raven, NEVERMORE”.

I had a winning night! Made this to accompany Chef John’s Simple Garlic Shrimp from this site + Spinach Salad II. This was FANTASTIC! I used half a box of Fideo (basically pre-chopped spaghetti) and did need 2c chicken broth - but I had been warned by other reviewers and prepared accordingly. I also added chopped dried onions halfway through and used dried parsley instead of fresh. This was a hit! This was so delicious (yet simple!) I can already imagine all the new recipes I plan to accompany this with! So in other words? I will be making again and again! Thanks so much Chef John!
Fantastic dish! Easy to make. Added sundried tomatoes, fresh mushrooms, asparagus, rotisserie chicken and shrimp.
This came out way better than I imagined and my family now asks for it as a side dish. I broke my own pasta and used shredded jack cheese.

I was looking for something different pasta wise and this looked intriguing. It was really good but took at least 20 minutes to cook and used at least 3.5 cups chicken broth to get cooked. I’ll make it again.
